# Pin how the clock component turns a time into hand angles

> [!NOTE]
> **Open for anyone.** The #18985 first-timer reservation ended on 2026-10-31. Claim this issue with a comment.
> The witness lives in the **component tier**: it tests something a person looks at, and #18985's tier rule sends those to a real browser.

## Welcome 👋

`Neo.component.Clock` draws an analog clock with CSS: set `time: '03:30'` and it rotates two hands. The maths is four lines of school geometry, and nothing pins it yet. This is a friendly first spec: mount the component in a real browser, then compare numbers in its DOM.

This is a **good first issue**. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone). The component tier starts its own server and builds the themes it needs on its first run.

## Where things live

- **Source:** `src/component/Clock.mjs` (ntype `clock`). The component's first child element is the minute hand and its second is the hour hand. Each hand gets an inline `transform` of `rotate(<deg>deg)`.
- **New test file:** `test/playwright/component/component/Clock.spec.mjs`
- **Pattern to copy:** `test/playwright/component/component/Image.spec.mjs`. It mounts a component into the empty test viewport with `Neo.worker.App.createNeoInstance`, reads the real DOM, and destroys the component afterwards. To change a config on the mounted clock, use `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs({id, ...})`, as `test/playwright/component/component/Base.spec.mjs` does.

## What to cover

| Config | Expected in the DOM |
|---|---|
| `time: '03:30'` | minute hand `transform: rotate(180deg)`, hour hand `rotate(105deg)` |
| `time: '15:45'` | minute hand `rotate(270deg)`, hour hand `rotate(112.5deg)`: hours wrap at 12 |
| `time: '12:00'` | both hands `rotate(0deg)` |
| `size: 300` | the clock's inline `height` and `width` are `300px` |
| `size` set to a non-number (e.g. `'50%'`) | the inline `height` and `width` are empty |
| `showDisc: false`, then `true` | the clock loses the `neo-show-disc` class, then regains it |
| `fontSize: 30` | the clock's inline `font-size` is `30px` |

The formulas, from the source:
- hour angle: `30 * (hours % 12) + 0.5 * minutes`
- minute angle: `6 * minutes`

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/component/component/Clock.spec.mjs` exists and follows the pattern file's setup and teardown.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row.
- [ ] The change is test-only, with one known exception. `Clock#afterSetSize` removes the size with `delete`. On a single-node component that reverts to the value leaked into `wrapperStyle` (see the `style_` docblock in `component.Base`), so the non-number row fails at runtime: `500px` instead of empty. Set `style.height` and `style.width` to `null` there instead, as `component.Base#show` does for `visibility`. If the component disagrees with any other row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/component/Clock.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-components` passes.

## Out of scope

Styling, animation, and a live ticking clock.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine. In Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things are worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-06T06:39:03Z

**Author ruling on the non-number `size` row** (re https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19131#issuecomment-6678854379):

The row states the intended contract, and the runtime `500px` is a bug in `Clock`, not a stale expectation.

`Clock#afterSetSize` clears the size with `delete style.height` / `delete style.width`. The `style_` docblock in `component.Base` documents exactly this trap: on a single-node component (`vdom === vdomRoot`), removing a style property requires `null`, because `delete` "will revert to the previous state, which unfortunately includes the very value you are trying to remove if it has leaked into `wrapperStyle`". `beforeGetWrapperStyle` merges `vdom.style` back in, and `updateStyle` spreads `wrapperStyle` under `style`, so the deleted keys come back. `component.Base#show` already follows the rule, with `style.visibility = null`.

The fix is two lines in `afterSetSize`: set `style.height` and `style.width` to `null`. The body's "Done when" now names that one exception to test-only. The fix stays in this ticket rather than becoming a micro-ticket, and the failing row then turns green on the source change.
